{"notes": "Visit 4 (6:15). The picture still shows both problems from 2:45 and 5:00. (1) The pale cluster at ~23-24, 8.5-9.3 on the upper tail is still disconnected, so the upper tail past the crossing will probably not topple from the start. (2) The belly line is still doubled around 19-22, 11-13. I don't know who placed which domino, so I can't attribute either problem to anyone. At 5:45 the team called it done and nobody mentioned the gap or the doubling. I'll wait for the push result before judging.

Sofia: Said 'Ready when you are' and wanted to see it swim. She claimed the crossing-to-upper-tail section, and the gap is in or next to it. She also called the doubled joint 'fine' without checking. Her earlier leadership and collaboration credit stands (clear split, reassured Jack). Execution is unproven and a concern. Ask her what she placed last and whether she checked the gap.

Omar: Silent this visit. He offered earlier to nudge the off-to-side domino before the crossing, but I can't confirm he did it or whether the pale cluster is his. Don't rate him on guesses. Ask him directly. Low visibility is a collaboration question mark.

Hana: Took the crossing join, and the belly connects through it. She joined the countdown ('Hands off, here we go') but never mentioned the issues. Ask what she placed.

Jack: Inspector on the doubled joint. He cheered 'proper fish, great teamwork' while the doubling and gap were still visible. Either he didn't find them or didn't flag them. Warm and encouraging, but the inspection looks ineffective. Ask what he checked and told people.

Review: see how far the dominoes fall, then ask each person what they placed and who owned the gap."}
